title: Beyond Retrieval: Query-Conditioned Reuse of Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories

visual_explainer.blocker: Per-paper GPT Image backfill is blocked in this run because two fresh isolated ReFind renders ignored their paper-specific brief and produced an unrelated dashboard with fabricated metadata. After repeated generator-level paper-identity failure, no ungrounded QCR render was published.

analysis.tldr: QCR identifies a distinct post-retrieval bottleneck: once a relevant long trajectory has been selected, the agent still needs a target-bound representation that preserves reusable procedure while forcing stale source bindings to be reacquired from current state.
analysis.problem: Retrieving a successful trajectory does not specify how to reuse it when users, files, IDs, dates, constraints, or environment state have changed. Raw traces can cause source-specific values to displace current evidence, while generic source-only summaries may omit target-specific applicability and verification requirements.
analysis.core_idea: Hold retrieval and execution conditions fixed, then insert one post-retrieval transformation. From the selected trajectory, target query, and initial target observation, QCR writes a compact support object containing a workflow invariant, bindings to re-obtain, applicability conditions, and a verification guardrail. The actor must recover current target bindings instead of copying source values.

memory_design.write: Successful source trajectories are cached offline with compact descriptors used for retrieval and selection; generic summaries are source-only and built before the target query.
memory_design.organize: QCR does not replace the persistent store. It creates a target-bound support representation from one selected trajectory, separating reusable workflow from source-specific bindings and preserving applicability/verification constraints.
memory_design.read: A fixed top-5 embedding retriever and summary ranker select one reusable trajectory. The actor then receives no memory, the full trajectory, a generic summary, or QCR support under matched target/model/tool conditions.
memory_design.update_forget: The paper studies reuse of verified prior trajectories rather than online memory editing, consolidation, or forgetting.

compared_to: Direct injection of the same selected full trajectory
A length-matched generic source-only summary of the same historical record
No-memory execution under the same target state, actor, decoding, and tool budget
analysis.evidence: Across 2,391 WebArena, WorkArena, and AppWorld targets, QCR reaches 62.3% average Success, 10.7 points above Full Trajectory while using 9.4k online tokens versus 18.4k (-48.9%). Candidate selection is already strong: the ranker selects reusable history for 94.8% of targets and end-task success is only 1.8 points below an oracle reusable selector, making post-selection reuse a plausible remaining bottleneck. Under large binding shift, Full Trajectory produces stale-binding errors on 46.9% of targets versus 10.9% for QCR; correct rebinding rises 31.7%→77.8%. QCR retains +20.1 points of utility under large shift versus +2.2 for Full Trajectory.
analysis.why_it_matters: This adds a missing boundary to the memory pipeline: storage → retrieval → selection is still not enough for long procedural memories. The representation delivered to the actor must be adapted to current state, and a complete source trace may be a worse interface than a compact support object even when retrieval is correct.
limitations: The evaluation uses successful source trajectories, one selected memory, and controlled source-target rewrites; natural recurring histories, partial failures, and multi-memory composition are not studied.
QCR's four-field schema is not individually ablated, so the experiment supports target-conditioned reuse as an operation more strongly than this exact schema.
Binding-shift analyses are associative across task groups except for the direct annotation of stale/correct rebinding; task difficulty differs across length groups.
Verified completion does not measure irreversible side effects or policy violations caused by trajectory reuse.
